items.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I went right on and stayed there at Purdue because Paul Reegy had the orchestra, and so I remember the second year we had a gig for the whole summer at Sylvania, Ohio

ctx.x: Were you anxious to get out of high school and get on with it?

Yes, really. I remember in fact I went to Purdue, there was a guy by the name of Paul Reegy was one of the youngest men, in engineering, in the faculty at Purdue, I think he © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

was 27, and he was on the faculty. And he played piano. And he was into logarithms and all that. Figuratively speaking, you know, he had a college band. And first of all I used to ride my bicycle up to the high school, which was about a mile away on Lincoln Way, which is the big main drag from Mishawaka, every Friday we used to play for dances. And I played all the jazz. And I remember having my tux and rolling up my pants so it wouldn’t get caught in the chain, and my trumpet, and getting down there I’d get off…
